evidence.claim: Social safety-net spending was budgeted at 3.2 percent of GDP in FY22; expanded programs included widow and old-age allowances, a new urban-poor database, and cash transfers totaling Tk 27 billion for about 9 million people, with G2P and mobile-finance tools used to improve transparency and reach.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: 2021 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: Social safety-net spending was budgeted at 3.2 percent of GDP in FY22; expanded programs included widow and old-age allowances, a new urban-poor database, and cash transfers totaling Tk 27 billion for about 9 million people, with G2P and mobile-finance tools used to improve transparency and reach.
evidence.source_locator: Annex V / social safety net section in the search-result excerpt
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF staff report excerpt is highly relevant, though the full page was not directly fetchable in this environment.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers FY22 and the 2022 policy environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Bangladesh authorities under Hasina; the implementation channel was the finance and social protection apparatus.
contrary_evidence: The excerpt also says health and education spending remained low, so the social-protection gains did not erase broader financing gaps.

evidence.claim: Key elements of the program included higher revenue mobilization, spending rationalization, modernizing the monetary policy framework, and increasing exchange-rate flexibility.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with Bangladesh on the Extended Credit Facility/Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility
evidence.excerpt: Key elements of the program included higher revenue mobilization, spending rationalization, modernizing the monetary policy framework, and increasing exchange-rate flexibility.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF summary of the program's policy package, directly tied to 2022 decision-making.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Bangladesh authorities; implementation depended on the Hasina government and the central bank.
contrary_evidence: The need for a Fund program indicates that existing policy settings had not been sufficient on their own.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh raised fuel prices by about 50 percent, inflation was already above 7 percent, and foreign-exchange reserves had fallen to $39.67 billion from $45.89 billion a year earlier.
evidence.title: Bangladesh announces fuel price jump, stokes inflation fears
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh raised fuel prices by about 50 percent, inflation was already above 7 percent, and foreign-exchange reserves had fallen to $39.67 billion from $45.89 billion a year earlier.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters copy lines 428-452 in the Investing.com republication
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with specific price, inflation, and reserve figures; republication preserves the original wire content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Bangladesh government and energy ministry under Hasina.
contrary_evidence: Officials said the hike was unavoidable because of global market conditions, so the action was partly reactive rather than purely discretionary.

evidence.claim: The government appointed finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder as Bangladesh Bank governor; the article says he had held senior finance posts and specialized in public finance, budget reform, macroeconomic management, and IT in public financial management.
evidence.title: Bangladesh appoints Abdur Rouf Talukder as central bank governor
evidence.excerpt: The government appointed finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder as Bangladesh Bank governor; the article says he had held senior finance posts and specialized in public finance, budget reform, macroeconomic management, and IT in public financial management.
evidence.source_locator: Article body describing the appointment and career background
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting on a specific economic appointment with clear career details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers a 2022 appointment affecting monetary management.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Hasina government; the appointment was made through the finance ministry/government notification.
contrary_evidence: The appointee was a senior civil servant rather than an independent outside technocrat, so the appointment does not prove maximal autonomy.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh's growth was backed by decades of systematic investments in climate resilience and disaster preparedness; the country had reduced cyclone-related deaths by 100-fold since 1970, but the poorest would be hardest hit without further action.
evidence.title: Key Highlights: Country Climate and Development Report for Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh's growth was backed by decades of systematic investments in climate resilience and disaster preparedness; the country had reduced cyclone-related deaths by 100-fold since 1970, but the poorest would be hardest hit without further action.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank feature story with concrete, Bangladesh-specific claims and explicit distributional consequence language.
evidence.period_fit: Fits the 2022 climate-and-social-risk environment affecting household welfare.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is partly inherited/system-level credit rather than a discrete Hasina-only act, but it reflects the governing state's welfare and resilience choices.
contrary_evidence: It also warns that Bangladesh still faces severe and increasing climate risks.

evidence.claim: The budget set social safety-net spending at Tk 113,576 crore, or 16.75 percent of the budget and 2.55 percent of GDP, expanded G2P cash transfers to 26.3 million beneficiaries, and said roughly five crore low-income people would directly benefit from the initiative.
evidence.title: Budget Speech
evidence.excerpt: The budget set social safety-net spending at Tk 113,576 crore, or 16.75 percent of the budget and 2.55 percent of GDP, expanded G2P cash transfers to 26.3 million beneficiaries, and said roughly five crore low-income people would directly benefit from the initiative.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific numerical budget claim from a direct speech transcript, though accessed via a media republication rather than an official host page.
evidence.period_fit: Directly tied to the 2022-23 fiscal year and its 2022 implementation window.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Hasina government; it reflects allocative choices but not detailed district-level implementation.
contrary_evidence: Large allocations do not by themselves prove effective delivery or unbiased targeting.

evidence.claim: Hasina said the government would keep building houses for homeless people, that no one would remain landless or shelter-less, and that the Ashrayan project had just handed homes to 32,904 families.
evidence.title: No one to stay homeless in Bangladesh, PM declares after providing homes to about 33,000 destitute families
evidence.excerpt: Hasina said the government would keep building houses for homeless people, that no one would remain landless or shelter-less, and that the Ashrayan project had just handed homes to 32,904 families.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of a public speech with concrete beneficiary counts and explicit policy intent.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and directly about social-policy intent and delivery.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Sheikh Hasina as prime minister and project sponsor, though it remains a self-presented commitment rather than an independent audit.
contrary_evidence: Later evidence shows her family also benefited from secret plot allocations in 2022, which complicates the integrity picture.

evidence.claim: Hasina told parliament that giving land and houses to destitute people was one of the biggest joys of her life and framed housing the homeless as a core purpose of rule.
evidence.title: The biggest joy: PM breaks down in tears in parliament
evidence.excerpt: Hasina told parliament that giving land and houses to destitute people was one of the biggest joys of her life and framed housing the homeless as a core purpose of rule.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of a public statement, but the available access here is via snippet rather than a fully quoted archive page.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and directly about her public self-presentation on welfare and ethical purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Hasina as a personal statement, though it remains self-presentation rather than independent evidence of conduct.
contrary_evidence: Later plot-allocation evidence suggests the public welfare persona coexisted with private network benefit.

unresolved_gaps: No direct Hasina-specific 2022 decision on nuclear safety appointments, command-and-control, or emergency doctrine.
No independent audit of Rooppur safety performance or BAERA independence in the target year.
No direct Bangladesh-initiated interstate war, proxy war, or coercive military campaign in 2022.
Direct command-chain evidence for specific 2022 abuses remains thin.
Stronger direct evidence is still needed on institutional restraint, especially courts, election administration, and oversight bodies.
Household-level distribution and independent execution evidence are thinner than macro and program-announcement evidence.
Direct ruler causation for service delivery is thinner than outcome evidence.
Direct first-person evidence of correction, admission, or disclosure is still thin.
The plot-allocation/self-dealing allegations need stronger independent corroboration or final adjudication.
Independent audits of implementation quality and outcome progress are still limited compared with announced-program evidence.
Direct evidence that Hasina personally monitored, corrected, or replaced ineffective implementers is sparse.
